facts: SP-8119 warns that some materials are brittle at cryogenic temperatures and can lose ductility (become brittle) when exposed to cryogenic temperatures.

SP-8119 warns that differing coefficients of thermal expansion and differential thermal contraction (shrinkage) can result in large bolting problems, improper clearances or fits, and related alignment/seal problems when components contract at cryogenic temperatures; designers should use materials with similar coefficients of expansion and evaluate thermal movement.
payload.query: What two temperature-related material-selection concerns does NASA SP-8119 identify for cryogenic disconnects?
payload.answer:
Evidence-grounded answer:

- SP-8119 warns that some materials are brittle at cryogenic temperatures and can lose ductility (become brittle) when exposed to cryogenic temperatures. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed; nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 85-88, chunk 91eb9fc5]
- SP-8119 warns that differing coefficients of thermal expansion and differential thermal contraction (shrinkage) can result in large bolting problems, improper clearances or fits, and related alignment/seal problems when components contract at cryogenic temperatures; designers should use materials with similar coefficients of expansion and evaluate thermal movement. [nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 85-88, chunk 91eb9fc5; nasa-sp-8119.pdf, pp. 130-132, chunk 68fbe1ed]
